title: Multimodal prehabilitation reduces postoperative complications in highrisk patients undergoing major gastrointestinal cancer surgery – a multicentre, randomised, controlled trial
summary: Complications following major cancer surgery are still a significant problem. In an ageing society, increasingly also with numerous concomitant diseases, it is important to prepare patients adequately for major surgery in order to avoid complications after the operation and improve survival. Modern treatment concepts such as prehabilitation are the subject of current scientific research. In our study, we are investigating the influence of prehabilitation (physical training before surgery + nutritional optimization + psychological support) on the occurrence of moderate to severe complications after cancer surgery.

interventions.name: The intervention group will receive a supervised progressive exercise programme conducted and supervised by a professional sport therapist, consisting of three 50-min sessions per week. Each session will be divided in a resistance exercise part, aiming to increase patients’ strength and an endurance

Patients allocated to the control group will receive usual care that is representative of current medical practice. It will consist of advices on smoking cessation, reduction of alcohol intake and importance of exercise according to current guidelines for cancer patients of the American College of S

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Candidate to elective major gastrointestinal cancer surgery (pelvic exenteration, cytoreductive surgery, oesophagectomy, hepatectomy, pancreatectomy, rectum resection); 2) High risk for surgical complications defined by presence of comorbid disease such as deconditioning, heart disease, diabetes, renal impairment or morbid obesity; 3) Duke Activity Status Index score (DASI) <402; 5) Schedule allowing for at least 4 weeks for intervention with multimodal prehabilitation prior to surgery / willingness to exercise
Exclusion criteria:
1) Non-elective surgery; 2) Unstable cardiac or respiratory disease; 3) Locomotor limitations precluding exercise training; 4) Cognitive deterioration impeding adherence to the programme; 5) Enrolment in other research studies affecting study endpoint
